2802: of uncertain derivation; Claude, an island near Crete:--Clauda.
2803: feminine of Κλαύδιος; Claudia, a Christian woman:--Claudia.
2804: of Latin origin; Claudius, the name of two Romans:--Claudius.
2805: from κλαίω; lamentation:--wailing, weeping, X wept.
2806: a primary verb; to break (specially, of bread):--break.
2807: from κλείω; a key (as shutting a lock), literally or figuratively:--key.
2808: a primary verb; to close (literally or figuratively):--shut (up).
2809: from κλέπτω; stealing (properly, the thing stolen, but used of the act):--theft.
2810: probably contracted from (compound of κλέος and πατήρ); Cleopas, a Christian:--Cleopas.
2811: from a shorter form of καλέω; renown (as if being called):--glory.
2812: from κλέπτω; a stealer (literally or figuratively):--thief. Compare λῃστής.
2814: from κλάω; a limb or shoot (as if broken off):--branch.
2815: of Latin origin; merciful; Clemes (i.e. Clemens), a Christian:--Clement.
2816: from κληρονόμος; to be an heir to (literally or figuratively):--be heir, (obtain by) inherit(-ance).
2817: from κληρονόμος; heirship, i.e. (concretely) a patrimony or (genitive case) a possession:--inheritance.
2818: from κλῆρος and the base of νόμος (in its original sense of partitioning, i.e. (reflexively) getting by apportionment); a sharer by lot, i.e. inheritor (literally or figuratively); by implication, a possessor:--heir.
2819: probably from κλάω (through the idea of using bits of wood, etc., for the purpose; a die (for drawing chances); by implication, a portion (as if so secured); by extension, an acquisition (especially a patrimony, figuratively):--heritage, inheritance, lot, part.
2820: from κλῆρος; to allot, i.e. (figuratively) to assign (a privilege):--obtain an inheritance.
2821: from a shorter form of καλέω; an invitation (figuratively):--calling.
2822: from the same as κλῆσις; invited, i.e. appointed, or (specially), a saint:--called.
2823: of uncertain derivation; an earthen pot used for baking in:--oven.
2824: from κλίνω; a slope, i.e. (specially) a "clime" or tract of country:--part, region.
2825: from κλίνω; a couch (for sleep, sickness, sitting or eating):--bed, table.
2826: neuter of a presumed derivative of κλίνη; a pallet or little couch:--bed.
2827: a primary verb; to slant or slope, i.e. incline or recline (literally or figuratively):--bow (down), be far spent, lay, turn to flight, wear away.
2828: from a derivative of κλίνω; properly, reclination, i.e. (concretely and specially), a party at a meal:--company.
2830: from (to billow or dash over); a surge of the sea (literally or figuratively):--raging, wave.
2831: middle voice from κλύδων; to surge, i.e. (figuratively) to fluctuate:--toss to and fro.
2832: of Chaldee origin (corresponding to אַחְאָב); Clopas, an Israelite:--Cleophas.
2833: from a primary (to scrape); to scratch, i.e. (by implication) to tickle:--X itching.
2834: probably of foreign origin; Cnidus, a place in Asia Minor:--Cnidus.
2835: of Latin origin; a quadrans, i.e. the fourth part of an as:--farthing.
2836: from ("hollow"); a cavity, i.e. (especially) the abdomen; by implication, the matrix; figuratively, the heart:--belly, womb.
2837: from κεῖμαι; to put to sleep, i.e. (passively or reflexively) to slumber; figuratively, to decease:--(be a-, fall a-, fall on) sleep, be dead.
2838: from κοιμάω; sleeping, i.e. (by implication) repose:--taking of rest.
2839: probably from σύν; common, i.e. (literally) shared by all or several, or (ceremonially) profane:--common, defiled, unclean, unholy.
2840: from κοινός; to make (or consider) profane (ceremonially):--call common, defile, pollute, unclean.
2841: from κοινωνός; to share with others (objectively or subjectively):--communicate, distribute, be partaker.
2842: from κοινωνός; partnership, i.e. (literally) participation, or (social) intercourse, or (pecuniary) benefaction:--(to) communicate(-ation), communion, (contri-)distribution, fellowship.
2843: from κοινωνός; communicative, i.e. (pecuniarily) liberal:--willing to communicate.
2844: from κοινός; a sharer, i.e. associate:--companion, X fellowship, partaker, partner.
2845: from κεῖμαι; a couch; by extension, cohabitation; by implication, the male sperm:--bed, chambering, X conceive.
2847: from κόκκος (from the kernel-shape of the insect); crimson-colored:--scarlet (colour, coloured).
2848: apparently a primary word; a kernel of seed:--corn, grain.
2849: from (dwarf); properly, to curtail, i.e. (figuratively) to chastise (or reserve for infliction):--punish.
2850: from a derivative of (a fawner); flattery:-- X flattering.
2852: from a derivative of the base of κολάζω; to rap with the fist:--buffet.
2853: from ("glue"); to glue, i.e. (passively or reflexively) to stick (figuratively):--cleave, join (self), keep company.
2854: neuter of a presumed derivative of (a cake; prob akin to the base of κολλάω); properly, a poultice (as made of or in the form of crackers), i.e. (by analogy) a plaster:-- eyesalve.
2855: from a presumed derivative of (a small coin; probably akin to κολλούριον); a coin-dealer:--(money-)changer.
2856: from a derivative of the base of κολάζω; to dock, i.e. (figuratively) abridge:--shorten.
2857: apparently feminine plural of kolossos ("colossal"); Colossæ, a place in Asia Minor:--Colosse.
2858: from Κολοσσαί; a Colossæan, (i.e. inhabitant of Colossæ:--Colossian.
2859: apparently a primary word; the bosom; by analogy, a bay:--bosom, creek.
2860: from (a diver); to plunge into water:--swim.
2861: from κολυμβάω; a diving-place, i.e. pond for bathing (or swimming):--pool.
2862: of Latin origin; a Roman "colony" for veterans:--colony.
2863: from κόμη; to wear tresses of hair:--have long hair.
2864: apparently from the same as κομίζω; the hair of the head (locks, as ornamental, and thus differing from θρίξ; which properly denotes merely the scalp):--hair.
2865: from a primary (to tend, i.e. take care of); properly, to provide for, i.e. (by implication) to carry off (as if from harm; genitive case obtain):--bring, receive.
2866: neuter comparative of a derivative of the base of 2865 (meaning, properly, well dressed, i.e. nice); figuratively, convalescent:--+ began to amend.
2867: from (dust; by analogy, lime); to whitewash:--whiten.
2868: from the base of κονιάω and ornumi (to "rouse"); pulverulence (as blown about):--dust.
2869: from κόπος; to tire, i.e. (figuratively) to relax:--cease.
2870: from κόπτω; mourning (properly, by beating the breast):--lamentation.
2872: from a derivative of κόπος; to feel fatigue; by implication, to work hard:--(bestow) labour, toil, be wearied.
2873: from κόπτω; a cut, i.e. (by analogy) toil (as reducing the strength), literally or figuratively; by implication, pains:--labour, + trouble, weariness.
2874: from (ordure; perhaps akin to κόπτω); manure:--dung(-hill).
2875: a primary verb; to "chop"; specially, to beat the breast in grief:--cut down, lament, mourn, (be-)wail. Compare the base of τομώτερος.
2876: perhaps from κορέννυμι; a crow (from its voracity):--raven.
2877: neuter of a presumed derivative of (a maiden); a (little) girl:--damsel, maid.
2878: of Hebrew and Chaldee origin respectively (קׇרְבָּן); a votive offering and the offering; a consecrated present (to the Temple fund); by extension (the latter term) the Treasury itself, i.e. the room where the contribution boxes stood:--Corban, treasury.
2879: of Hebrew origin (קֹרַח); Core (i.e. Korach), an Israelite:--Core.
2880: a primary verb; to cram, i.e. glut or sate:--eat enough, full.
2881: from Κόρινθος; a Corinthian, i.e. inhabitant of Corinth:--Corinthian.
2882: of uncertain derivation; Corinthus, a city of Greece:--Corinth.
2883: of Latin origin; Cornelius, a Roman:--Cornelius.
2884: of Hebrew origin (כֹּר); a cor, i.e. a specific measure:--measure.
2885: from κόσμος; to put in proper order, i.e. decorate (literally or figuratively); specially, to snuff (a wick):--adorn, garnish, trim.
2886: from κόσμος (in its secondary sense); terrene ("cosmic"), literally (mundane) or figuratively (corrupt):--worldly.
2887: from κόσμος (in its primary sense); orderly, i.e. decorous:--of good behaviour, modest.
2888: from κόσμος and κρατέω; a world-ruler, an epithet of Satan:--ruler.
2889: probably from the base of κομίζω; orderly arrangement, i.e. decoration; by implication, the world (in a wide or narrow sense, including its inhabitants, literally or figuratively (morally)):--adorning, world.
2890: of Latin origin (fourth); Quartus, a Christian:--Quartus.
2892: of Latin origin; "custody", i.e. a Roman sentry:--watch.
2895: probably of foreign origin; a mattress:--bed.
2896: a primary verb; properly, to "croak" (as a raven) or scream, i.e. (genitive case) to call aloud (shriek, exclaim, intreat):--cry (out).
2897: probably from the same as ἁρπάζω; properly, a headache (as a seizure of pain) from drunkenness, i.e. (by implication) a debauch (by analogy, a glut):--surfeiting.
2898: diminutive of a derivative of the base of κέρας; a skull ("cranium"):--Calvary, skull.
2899: of uncertain derivation; a margin, i.e. (specially), a fringe or tassel:--border, hem.
